cli.cmd_doctor: Check that every tool Bumpproof needs is installed and logged in
cli.cmd_init: Write .bumpproof/config.json and draft journeys for an app
cli.cmd_check: Compare the base and head of a bump in a real browser
cli.cmd_fix: Let the coding agent fix a regression, then verify again
cli.cmd_pr: Run the whole loop on a pull request

cli.not_built: The '{name}' command is not built yet.
cli.disabled: Bumpproof is disabled in config ("enabled": false). Nothing to do.
cli.opt_base: Base ref for check (branch, tag or commit)
cli.opt_dir: App folder inside the repository (default: config app.dir)
cli.opt_canary: With fix: run the canary test that decides host or container mode for the fixer
cli.opt_out: report: folder to write the site to (default docs)
cli.opt_comment: report: print the pull request comment for one run folder
cli.opt_speed: replay: recorded seconds per real second (0 = no pauses)
cli.opt_markdown: with check: also write a pull request comment in Markdown to this file
cli.opt_min_free_gb: with check: refuse to start below this much free disk (GB)
cli.bad_number: {option} needs a number of zero or more, got "{value}".
cli.opt_find: Find census candidates and write the list (no Kane needed)
cli.opt_build_only: with check: build and start both sides only; skip the browser journeys
cli.opt_publish: with check: also write the run record to docs/runs/<id>/ for the report site
cli.opt_fix: with check: when the head regresses or does not build, let the fixer patch it and replay the journeys
cli.opt_push_fix: with pr --fix: push a verified fix onto the pull request branch (our repositories only)
cli.opt_run: Run the next eligible census candidates (--limit n, --only owner/repo)

site.tagline: Dependency bumps, checked in a real browser before you merge.
site.hero_title: Dependabot says the bump is safe. Bumpproof makes Kane CLI prove it.
site.hero_body: Bumpproof builds your app twice in a Docker sandbox, once on the base branch and once on the bump. Kane CLI walks the same user journeys in Chrome against both. Plain code compares the runs. When the bump breaks a journey, Claude Code writes a fix and Kane CLI runs every journey again.
site.step_build_body: Each side is installed, built and served in a locked-down container on the same port.
site.step_kane_body: Kane CLI runs the same plain-English tests in Chrome against each side.
site.step_verdict_body: Exit codes and heal events decide: same, UI moved, or regression. No model decides.
site.step_fix_body: Claude Code edits files only. Guards check the patch. Kane CLI runs every journey again.
site.install_title: Run it on your own repository
site.install_body: Needs Node 20 or later, Docker, a Kane CLI login and Claude Code.
site.runs_empty: No runs recorded yet. Each run of bumpproof check or bumpproof pr adds one here.
site.status_body: Built during the KaneCLI Online Hackathon (12 to 26 November 2026). Every number on these pages is read from the JSON files in the repository.
site.synthetic: Synthetic example made for tests. Not a real run.
site.run_shots_note: Screenshots Kane CLI took at the step that failed on the pull request, and at the same step on the base branch and after the fix. Nothing else from the evidence pack is published. Select a screenshot to open it at full size.
site.run_replay: Replay this run in a terminal (no keys, no credits)
site.run_facts: Time {time} · {credits} Kane CLI credits · Kane CLI {kane}

action.no_journeys: This Action builds and starts the base and this pull request in a locked-down Docker container. It does not run browser journeys or fixes, and it holds no LLM key. For Kane CLI journeys and fixes, run `bumpproof pr <owner>/<repo>#<number> --fix` on your own machine.

readme.table_intro: Each row is one `bumpproof pr … --fix --publish --comment` run on a pull request Dependabot opened on this repository. On #1 and #2 the verified fix was also pushed (`--push-fix`). #3 was left as Dependabot opened it, so the break can still be reproduced. Nothing was merged.
